```{r compute}
# values quoted below; same seeds and settings as the Act keys
f2 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 2)
f3 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 3)

bd <- read.csv("../data/BdPondSurvey.csv")
temp <- bd$water_temp_c
swabbed <- bd$frogs_swabbed
positive <- bd$bd_positive
log_post <- function(par, x = temp) {
  sum(dbinom(positive, swabbed, plogis(par[1] + par[2] * x), log = TRUE)) +
    sum(dnorm(par, 0, 10, log = TRUE))
}
metropolis <- function(start, step_sd, n_steps, x = temp) {
  chain <- matrix(NA, n_steps, 2)
  current <- start
  lp_current <- log_post(current, x)
  n_accept <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(n_steps)) {
    proposal <- current + rnorm(2, 0, step_sd)
    lp_prop <- log_post(proposal, x)
    if (log(runif(1)) < lp_prop - lp_current) {
      current <- proposal
      lp_current <- lp_prop
      n_accept <- n_accept + 1
    }
    chain[i, ] <- current
  }
  attr(chain, "accept_rate") <- n_accept / n_steps
  chain
}
burn <- seq_len(1000)
runs_raw <- lapply(1:2, function(s) { set.seed(s); metropolis(c(0, 0), c(0.2, 0.05), 10000) })
runs_cen <- lapply(1:2, function(s) { set.seed(s); metropolis(c(0, 0), c(0.2, 0.05), 10000, temp - 17) })
ci <- function(ch) paste(f2(quantile(ch[-burn, 2], c(0.025, 0.975))), collapse = " to ")
nll <- function(par, x) -sum(dbinom(positive, swabbed, plogis(par[1] + par[2] * x), log = TRUE))
fit <- optim(c(0, 0), nll, x = temp - 17, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
wald <- fit$par[2] + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * sqrt(solve(fit$hessian)[2, 2])
check_diff <- log_post(c(1, -0.1)) - log_post(c(3, -0.2))
acc_raw <- mean(sapply(runs_raw, attr, "accept_rate"))
acc_cen <- mean(sapply(runs_cen, attr, "accept_rate"))
```

# How to prepare (for students)

- **Big picture.** Monday turned simulated annealing into the
  Metropolis algorithm, a way to draw samples from a posterior without
  ever computing Bayes' denominator. In this lab you run a chain by
  hand, learn to tell a trustworthy chain from an untrustworthy one,
  and then write your own sampler for a two-parameter model of chytrid
  fungus in frogs.
- **Review:** the Metropolis acceptance rule from Monday's lecture
  (and why a rejected step still gets recorded); the Beta-binomial
  posterior from Week 8; the logistic model and centering a predictor
  from Lab 6, Act 1.
- **Read:** Bolker 7.3 through 7.3.2 (MCMC, burn-in, convergence,
  printed p. 310-315).
- **R skills:** writing a function, `for` loops, `rnorm()`,
  `runif()`, storing results in a matrix row by row, `quantile()`.

# Overview (instructor only)

| Beat | Mode | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Opening | BOARD | ~10 min |
| Act 1 (closed laptop) | paper | ~55 min |
| Act 2 Part 1 + group plan check | paper | ~30 min |
| Act 2 Part 2 (laptops) | laptop | rest of period; finish at home |

**Goal for the period:** every group finishes Act 1, and every student
leaves with an Act 2 plan their group has checked. Monday had no WOD,
so the opening is short; skip it entirely if Monday's discussion
(three germination chains) happened.

**Group time for Act 2 (announce it; the handout doesn't say it).**
Act 2 has to work as an individual take-home, so it has no group
language. When a group finishes Act 1, have them do Act 2's Part 1
(1a, 1b) on their own, then compare log posteriors and pseudocode as a
group for ~10 min before opening laptops. Things to listen for: priors
missing from 1a, a sign error turning it into an NLL, and pseudocode
that records only accepted steps.

**Data.** Act 1 is one pond (2 of 20, weak Beta(2, 8) prior from
nearby ponds, posterior Beta(4, 26)). Students add the log likelihood
and log prior from a printed table to get each log posterior. Act 2 is a 12-pond survey that includes that pond (P11). The
survey data are simulated (true $a = 2.2$, $b = -0.18$) and presented
as field results. Keys: `labs/answer_keys/Lab7_Act1_Key.Rmd`,
`Lab7_Act2_Key.Rmd`.

**Where this came from.** The Week 8 "if time" idea (reparameterize
to remove a strong parameter correlation) appears here as Act 2's
centering step. Bolker's 7.4 fitting checklist isn't used; it could
open Wednesday or a later lab.

# Part 1: Lab content

## Opening (~10 min) [BOARD]

- One-line workflow; point at **FIT**.
- Metropolis on the board, in log form: propose
  $\theta^* = \theta + \text{jump}$; accept if
  $\log u < \log P(\theta^* \mid y) - \log P(\theta \mid y)$; record
  the current value either way.
- Three things to check in any chain (only if Monday's discussion was
  cut): burn-in (trend at the start), jumps too small (slow creep, near
  100% accepted), jumps too big (flat stretches, few accepted). Runs
  from different starts should agree.
- Don't work an example with the lab's numbers. If students want one,
  use Monday's germination data (30 of 40).

## Act 1 [paper]

**1a answer** (start 0.30):

| Step | Proposal | Difference | Accept? | Record |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.22 | +1.78 | yes | 0.22 |
| 2 | 0.31 | $-2.03$ | no ($\log u = -0.85$) | 0.22 |
| 3 | 0.15 | +1.00 | yes | 0.15 |
| 4 | $-0.02$ | $-\infty$ | no | 0.15 |
| 5 | 0.19 | $-0.49$ | yes ($\log u = -1.20$) | 0.19 |
| 6 | 0.08 | +0.58 | yes | 0.08 |

(Log posteriors: 0.30 is $-3.02$, 0.22 is $-1.24$, 0.31 is $-3.27$,
0.15 is $-0.24$, 0.19 is $-0.73$, 0.08 is $-0.15$.)

**Sticking points:** after the step 2 rejection, students start step 3
from 0.31 (ask "where is the chain right now?"); and some use only the
log likelihood column and forget to add the log prior.

- **1b:** skipping rejections drops the repeats that weight the peak;
  chain too spread out.
- **1c:** constants cancel in the difference. That's Monday's $P(y)$
  point again.
- **2a:** A good; B fine after ~150 steps of burn-in; C jumps too big
  (about 4% accepted, sticky); D jumps too small, two runs never meet.
- **2c:** credible 0.04 to 0.27 (mean 0.13), lopsided, above 0, and
  pulled up a little by the prior; Wald $-0.03$ to 0.23. Histogram
  should match Beta(4, 26).

## Act 2 [paper $\to$ laptop]

- **2a check value:** `r f2(check_diff)` (a difference, so dropped
  constants don't matter). A value of +`r f2(-check_diff)` means
  they coded the negative log posterior.
- **2b, raw temperature:** ~`r round(100 * acc_raw)`% accepted; two
  runs give e.g. `r ci(runs_raw[[1]])` and `r ci(runs_raw[[2]])`. The
  runs disagree, which is the point.
- **2c, centered:** ~`r round(100 * acc_cen)`% accepted; runs agree
  (`r ci(runs_cen[[1]])`, `r ci(runs_cen[[2]])`). Why: raw $a$ is the
  log-odds at 0 °C, so $a$ and $b$ trade off (correlation about
  $-0.97$); independent jumps fall off the ridge. Same as the Lab 6
  beetle dose and Monday's myxo banana.
- **2d:** Wald `r f2(wald[1])` to `r f2(wald[2])`; agrees with the
  credible interval to ~0.01.
- **Common bugs:** current log posterior not updated after an
  acceptance (acceptance rate drifts toward 100%); storing only on
  acceptance; `quantile()` over the whole matrix; same seed for both
  runs.
- **Reflection target:** many data and no boundary, so the intervals
  agree; Act 1 had few data near $p = 0$, so they didn't.

# PART 2: CIRCULATING CHEAT SHEET

\normalsize
\textit{Terse on purpose. Detail: Part 1 and the keys.}
\large

## Opening (~10 min) [BOARD]

- Workflow; point at **FIT**
- Accept if $\log u <$ lp(prop.) $-$ lp(curr.); **record either way**
- If Monday's discussion was cut: burn-in, too small, too big, runs agree
- Examples: germination (30 of 40) only, never the lab's numbers

\newpage

## Act 1 (~55 min) [paper]

- Records: 0.22, 0.22, 0.15, 0.15, 0.19, 0.08
- lp = log lik. + **log prior** (both from the table)
- Step 3 starts from **0.22**, not 0.31
- Step 4 ($-0.02$): reject, posterior 0
- 1c: constants cancel
- A good; B burn ~150; C too big; D too small, runs apart
- Credible 0.04-0.27 vs. Wald $-0.03$-0.23; Beta(4, 26)

\newpage

## Act 2 (rest of period) [paper $\to$ laptop]

- **After Act 1:** Part 1 alone, then ~10 min group compare before laptops
- Listen for: no priors; NLL sign; records only acceptances
- 2a check: `r f2(check_diff)`
- Raw: ~`r round(100 * acc_raw)`% accepted, runs disagree
- Centered: ~`r round(100 * acc_cen)`%, runs agree, $b$ about `r ci(runs_cen[[1]])`
- Wald `r f2(wald[1])` to `r f2(wald[2])`
- Bugs: lp not updated; store only on accept; same seed twice
